title: Defense witness grilled over ‘useless’ testimony
summary: Lawyer Rainer Dela Fuente cites confidentiality to explain why he did not review prosecution witness Alex Cabrera's forensic report, prompting criticisms from several senator-judges

MANILA, Philippines – A defense witness admitted that he had not read the prosecution’s financial forensic report or reviewed its supporting documents before testifying in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte on Thursday, November 19.
Lawyer Rainer Dela Fuente, a former Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) financial investigator, was presented as an expert witness for the defense on Day 44 of the trial.
During his direct examination, defense lawyer Mark Vinluan sought to challenge the methodology and findings of the financial forensic report prepared by prosecution witness Alex Cabrera.

blocks.caption: Financial analyst tells impeach court: Sara Duterte has P817M in undisclosed wealth

blocks.text: Dela Fuente, however, told the impeachment court that he had not been provided copies of the report and its supporting documents before the hearing.

“No, Your Honor,” Dela Fuente said when asked whether he had received copies of AMLC records, bank statements, insurance placements, and general information sheets (GIS) of companies linked to Duterte.
Vinluan confirmed that the witness had not reviewed the entire report, saying the defense intended to focus on specific portions of the 50-page document.
“If he is to refute the report, then he should have seen the report, should have read the report,” Senator-judge Joel Villanueva said.
“Now if he cannot answer these questions then, for me, it’s going to be useless,” Villanueva added.
Other senator-judges, including Erwin Tulfo, also questioned how Dela Fuente could examine the report’s findings without reviewing the underlying documents.

“Kung hindi naman niya po nakita pala ay mga dokumento, STRs (Suspicious Transaction Reports), CTRs (Covered Transaction Reports), what good is it? Para anong tetestigo niya, eh puro ito theory sa kanyang paningin, sa kanyang paniniwala,” Tulfo said.
(If has has not seen the documents, STRs, CTRs, what good is it? What’s his testimony for, it’ll just be all his theory, his beliefs.)
He added: “The witnesses you’ve been presenting here these past few days are weak. Get somebody who can really stand up, who can really answer questions from the senator-judges.”
Dela Fuente was listed as a defense witness who would testify on fundamental legal concepts under the Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA).

Explaining why he did not review the report and its supporting documents, Dela Fuente cited confidentiality concerns. He also said he was not dismissing Cabrera’s findings but was merely answering the defense’s hypothetical questions based on his understanding of the law.

“Ang akin lang pong saligan ay ang ating AMLA, ang ating batas, so I can answer based on the law… Ako personally, ayoko basahin yung report because coming here, and wala rin ako access sa report, coming here and reading that report, I will develop biases,” Dela Fuente said.

(My only basis is our AMLA, and our laws, so I can answer based on the law… Personally, I don’t want to read the report because coming here, and I also did not have access to the report, coming here here and reading that report, I will develop biases.)
The prosecution tried to paint Dela Fuente as unqualified.

“Your claimed expertise as a financial expert in financial investigation only comes from the 25 months that you were an entry-level investigator for the AMLC. Is that correct?” Diokno asked Dela Fuente, who answered in the affirmative.

Dela Fuente also admitted that he was not challenging the accuracy or truthfulness of the AMLC reports, Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) records, and bank records involving the Vice President.
Diokno, like the senators, also made a big deal of the fact that Dela Fuente did not read the forensic examination report prepared by the prosecution’s witness, Alexander Cabrera.

“Let’s say that I were going to evaluate your investigation report,” Diokno said. “If in my evaluation, I decide not to read everything and pick portions only, don’t you think it will be unfair to you?”
“You didn’t read the whole report. Wouldn’t you agree that context means a lot in terms of evaluating the veracity of a financial report?” Diokno added.

Cabrera previously testified that based on his analysis of the Vice President’s bank and financial records, Duterte, and her husband, Mans Carpio, had accumulated P817 million unexplained wealth from 2022 to 2025.
Duterte is being tried for Article II of the Articles of Impeachment, which involves allegations of unexplained wealth. – with reports from Dwight de Leon/Rappler.com
